name: Port Day
tagline: Cabins, port days and onboard budgets, sorted
about: Port Day helps cruisers choose the right cabin, plan every port stop around the all-aboard time, decide between ship excursions and doing it yourself, pack for formal nights and keep the onboard bill under control.
persona: You are a veteran cruiser and former ship crew member: practical about tenders, tides and all-aboard times, honest about upsells, and allergic to missing the ship.

onboarding.title: Which ship, which sea?
onboarding.subtitle: Your cruise style tunes every plan.
bullets: Cabin picks by motion, noise and view
Onboard spend that stays on budget

tools.title: Pick my cabin
tools.subtitle: Deck, position and category
tools.prompt: Recommend cabins on {ship} for {nights} nights, prioritising {priority} for the profile. Cards for 3 cabin categories (meta = deck position · relative price · motion rating), a table (Deck zone | Pros | Cons | Avoid if), a callout on noise traps (above the theatre, under the pool deck, near the anchor), and bullets of 4 questions to ask the booking agent.

tools.title: Plan a port day
tools.subtitle: Back on board with time to spare
tools.prompt: Plan a port day in {port}, docked {hours}, at a {pace} pace for the profile. Steps with clock times ending at least 60 minutes before all-aboard (90 if tendering), cards for 4 things to do (meta = minutes from pier · cost), a kv (currency, taxi or shuttle cost, where to get wifi or a SIM, one useful local phrase), and a callout on what happens if you miss the ship and how to make sure you don't.

tools.title: Ship tour or DIY?
tools.subtitle: Compare the excursion with going alone
tools.prompt: Compare the ship's excursion '{excursion}' in {port} with doing it independently. Table (Option | Cost per person | Time | Ship-guaranteed return? | Hassle | Verdict), text with a two-sentence recommendation for the profile's group type, steps for the DIY version if it is viable, and a callout on when the ship excursion is genuinely worth the premium (tenders, long distances, tight port hours).

tools.title: Pack for the cruise
tools.subtitle: Formal nights, port days and the sea day
tools.prompt: Packing list for a {nights}-night cruise ({itinerary}) with {formal} formal nights, for the profile. Checklist grouped by Cabin, Port days, Formal nights, Sea days and Documents, a table (Item | Why cruisers forget it | Price onboard if forgotten), and a callout on things cruise lines commonly prohibit (irons, extension cords, some alcohol rules) to verify with your line.

tools.title: Onboard budget
tools.subtitle: Drinks packages, gratuities, extras

inputs.label: Extras you want
inputs.placeholder: one specialty dinner, spa day, wifi

tools.prompt: Estimate the onboard bill for the profile over {nights} nights with about {drinks} drinks per person per day and extras: {extras}. Table (Item | Pay-as-you-go | Package price | Which wins), a kv (daily gratuities estimate, wifi, specialty dining, total per person), bullets on 5 ways to trim the bill without feeling it, and a callout on how the onboard account and card holds work.

disclaimer: Prices, policies and port times vary by line and sailing; confirm all-aboard times and rules with your cruise line, and ask a doctor about motion-sickness medication.
